clue.text: Intimidated, we drove criminal across America

indicators.note: across means the shuffled letters stretch over and around the letter for America
criminal suggests the words we drove are bent out of their proper order

explanation.surface: Someone frightened after a crime in which they and others drove across America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges WEDROVE into OVERWED, and 'across' puts that around A, giving OVER-A-WED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overawed is to be cowed or daunted, a close synonym of intimidated.

clue.text: Pure lady loses one pound

indicators.note: loses says a letter is taken away from the lady's name

parts.note: Virginia is a lady's name
I is the Roman numeral for one
L stands for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A virtuous woman loses a pound in weight or money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes the final I off VIRGINIA, leaving VIRGINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginal means chaste or untouched, so innocent and pure.

clue.text: Type of storage facility with irregular entry

parts.note: random means irregular, without pattern
access means entry or a way in

explanation.surface: A storage unit that people get into at odd times.
explanation.definitionFit: Random access memory is computer storage whose locations can be read in any order.

clue.text: Notes contents of this small case

definitions.text: Notes contents of this small case

parts.words: Notes contents of this small case
parts.note: the case is a small one that holds banknotes in a pocket

explanation.surface: A list of what a small case holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' seems to be a verb, as in listing; it is banknotes, which fill this case.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallet is a small flat folding case for carrying paper money and cards.

clue.text: Contents of cylinder, viscous fuel

indicators.note: contents of says the answer sits inside the following words, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A cylinder holding thick fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV is British diesel fuel for road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: DERV is diesel oil for road vehicles, so it is a type of fuel.

clue.text: Listen twice to exclamation of approval

indicators.note: twice says the word for listen is written a second time straight after the first

parts.note: to hear is to listen

explanation.surface: Being told to listen twice to a cry of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled call is how MPs in the House of Commons voice agreement with a speaker.

clue.text: Keen about replacing motion, not second

indicators.note: replacing is read as re-placing, putting the remaining letters in new places
not says the word for a second is left out of motion

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: An enthusiast for swapping a motion, though not one that was seconded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes MO from MOTION, leaving TION, which 'replacing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something, as into jazz, is informal for being enthusiastic about it.

clue.text: Endanger that erne fluttering

indicators.note: fluttering suggests the letters of that erne flap about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sea eagle in flight putting something at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: An erne is a sea eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: To threaten something is to put it at risk, which is to endanger it.

clue.text: Last team member, perhaps

parts.note: in a side of eleven players, such as cricket or football, the final one picked is numbered in this ordinal way

explanation.surface: A question about who comes at the bottom of a team's roster.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket and football teams have eleven players, so the last of them is the one with this ordinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal for the final place in an eleven-player side names that last member.

clue.text: Old king at home? Smile

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, a monarch of the past
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch relaxing in his palace allows himself a smile.
explanation.definitionFit: A grin is a broad smile, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Advice given by birth certificate?

parts.note: a commercial advice slip accompanying goods is read whimsically as a document recording a baby's arrival

explanation.surface: Wondering what guidance a birth certificate could give.
explanation.walkthrough: In commerce an 'advice' is a notification document; the one sent with goods is named after their delivery, which is also the word for a birth.
explanation.definitionFit: A document sent with goods to confirm their dispatch is an advice note; delivery doubles as childbirth.

clue.text: Was cautious after contract, unable to accept other opinions

indicators.note: after puts the cautious word behind the word for contract

parts.note: to narrow is to contract or become less wide
minded means took care, as in mind the step

explanation.surface: Someone careful after signing a deal but closed to other views.
explanation.definitionFit: Being narrow-minded is being intolerant of views that differ from one's own.

clue.text: Enlivened by article, I won on board

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
in chess, a player who wins on the board has checkmated, or mated, the opponent

explanation.surface: Someone livened up after an article reporting their win at a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated means full of life and spirit, the state of being enlivened.

clue.text: Just over four weeks with gold furnishings

parts.note: December, abbreviated Dec, lasts 31 days, slightly more than four weeks
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A month spent fitting a room with gilded furnishings.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the style of furnishing and decoration of a room.

clue.text: Wandering after word of hesitation, hurried by square

parts.note: er is the sound people make while hesitating
ran means hurried
a T-square is a drawing tool, so T can stand for square

explanation.surface: Someone drifting about after hesitating, then rushing past a town square.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant describes travelling in search of adventure, as a knight errant does, so roaming or wandering.

clue.text: Alliance building? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite says the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a block is a large building, such as an office block

explanation.surface: A question whether an alliance is nearly built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter K from BLOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations or parties combined in a common interest, an alliance.

clue.text: Restrict a railway line

parts.note: to bound is to restrict or set limits to

explanation.surface: An instruction to limit a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'railway line' looks like one phrase; 'line' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A boundary is a dividing line that marks a limit.

clue.text: Happen again to be somewhat more curious

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone finding themselves once again growing more inquisitive.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to occur again, so happen again is a direct synonym; 'to be' completes the verb phrase.

clue.text: Press person with regard to beer

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A journalist asking about beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is a journalist, someone who works for the press.

clue.text: Artillery in working port

indicators.note: in says the artillery letters sit inside the word for working

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Guns operating within a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Oran is a major Mediterranean seaport in Algeria, an example of a port.

clue.text: Turn up in notorious surroundings being overbearing

indicators.note: surroundings says the notorious word is placed around the reversed turn

parts.note: arrant means utter or notorious, as in an arrant rogue

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in your go

explanation.surface: A notorious figure showing up in their own surroundings and acting overbearingly.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the turn word bottom to top; 'Turn' is a noun (your go), not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogant means haughty and domineering, behaving with a sense of superiority.

clue.text: Mounting castle maintenance

parts.note: up means mounting or rising
a keep is the main tower of a castle

explanation.surface: The rising cost of looking after a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the cost or work of keeping something in good repair.

clue.text: One or two girls that might add taste

definitions.meaning: the name is one girl's name, or two girls' names, Rose and Mary, side by side
the aromatic herb is used to flavour food

explanation.surface: Girls who might bring some style to an occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is a woman's name made of two others, and a culinary herb that flavours lamb.

clue.text: Put peg in instrument

indicators.note: in says the peg goes inside the word for put

parts.note: to set is to put or place
a pin is a peg

explanation.surface: Fixing a tuning peg into a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord, a keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Stationer Sid revised thesis

indicators.note: revised suggests the letters of Stationer Sid are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A stationer called Sid went over a student's thesis again.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissertation is a long academic essay, the kind submitted as a thesis for a degree.

clue.text: Criticise winning every trick?

definitions.meaning: in bridge a ... is winning all thirteen tricks

explanation.surface: Censuring someone who takes every trick at cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Slam is slang for harsh criticism, and in card games like bridge a grand slam takes every trick.

clue.text: Drivers touring ancient city creating atmosphere

indicators.note: touring says the drivers go around the ancient city

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motorists' organisation
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Motorists visiting an ancient city and finding a special atmosphere there.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a distinctive feeling or air surrounding a place or person.

clue.text: Gloomy linesman sent back

indicators.note: sent back says the poet's word is read from right to left

parts.note: a bard writes lines of verse, so is a poet or linesman

explanation.surface: A dejected football official sent away by the referee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linesman' suggests a football official, but here it is a poet, a writer of lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab means dull and dreary, so cheerless or gloomy in appearance.

clue.text: Harvest fruit to crop up again

parts.note: to reap is to harvest a crop
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Gathering fruit so that the crop will come again next year.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappear is to show up once more, which is what crop up again means.

clue.text: Cure is found by worker for whom I have great affection

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker
to dote is to be extremely fond

explanation.surface: A remedy discovered by an employee the speaker adores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for whom' joins the worker to 'I have great affection', so it reads ANT, I DOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote counteracts a poison, so it is a remedy or cure.
